summary: The main article describes a dual Cu(I)/CPA-catalysed asymmetric radical aminofluoroalkylation of alkenes using various fluoroalkylsulfonyl chlorides. It includes 5 tables detailing optimization and substrate scope for perfluoroalkylation, difluoromethylation, and trifluoromethylation, along with 4 figures illustrating the proposal, synthetic transformations, and mechanistic studies.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Our proposal. Dual Cu(I)/CPA-catalysed asymmetric radical aminofluoroalkylation of alkenes.
items.description: This figure outlines the general reaction scheme for the intramolecular aminofluoroalkylation of alkenes using a copper and chiral phosphoric acid dual-catalytic system.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Optimization of reaction conditions.
items.description: This table summarizes the screening of bases, catalysts, and solvents to optimize the yield and enantioselectivity of the aminoperfluoroalkylation reaction.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Substrate scope for aminoperfluoroalkylation of 1*.
items.description: This table displays the scope of various N-alkenyl urea substrates and their corresponding yields and enantioselectivities for the aminoperfluoroalkylation process.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Substrate scope for aminodifluoro(methoxycarbonyl)methylation of 1*.
items.description: This table explores the substrate scope for the reaction using difluoro(methoxycarbonyl)methylsulfonyl chloride as the radical source.

items.heading: Table 4
items.caption: Substrate scope for aminodifluoromethylation of 1*.
items.description: This table details the results of the aminodifluoromethylation of various alkenes using difluoromethylsulfonyl chloride.

items.heading: Table 5
items.caption: Substrate scope for aminotrifluoromethylation of 1*.
items.description: This table shows the scope of the aminotrifluoromethylation reaction using trifluoromethanesulfonyl chloride as a cost-effective radical source.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Versatile transformations.
items.description: This figure demonstrates the synthetic utility of the products through reduction, hydrolysis, and cyclization reactions to form complex fluorinated molecules.

items.heading: Figure 3
items.caption: Mechanistic study.
items.description: This figure presents control experiments, including radical trapping and radical clock experiments, to support the proposed radical mechanism.

items.heading: Figure 4
items.caption: Mechanistic proposal. Two pathways were tentatively proposed.
items.description: This figure illustrates the proposed catalytic cycle involving Cu(I)/Cu(II)/Cu(III) intermediates and the role of the chiral phosphoric acid.
